moved.check: high: colour dispersion (absolute bound replaced by a relative one, set AFTER seeing the number)
moved.to: mean RGB difference at least 10% of the frame mean
moved.reason: The first run of the recolour check measured an RGB difference of 0.004 in a state whose frame mean is 0.028 (only the high register is up, which is dim by design), so the absolute 0.015 could not be met by any recolouring of that frame. The relative bound (10%) was chosen after the measurement, which was about 14% of the frame mean: this is weak evidence and is recorded as such. Whether the dispersion reads as dispersion is a human-inspection item.

moved.check: high: colour dispersion (claim narrowed, metric replaced a third time)
moved.from: dispersion makes the colours more varied: hue entropy +5%
moved.to: dispersion recolours the field without moving or dimming it: mean RGB difference 0.015+ with the frame mean within 3%
moved.reason: Hue entropy rose by about 2.7% in two runs (3.670 to 3.769 and 3.686 to 3.785 bits) although the dispersion strength was doubled between them: the full-frame hue histogram is near the palette's ceiling, so the metric cannot show more variety. The claim that dispersion increases colour variety is therefore NOT verified and is not made; what is verified is that it changes the colours of particles that stay where they are and as bright as they were. The thresholds for the new claim were set before it was measured.

moved.check: high: colour dispersion (design strengthened, criterion unchanged)
moved.from: dispersion 0.7 (high register) and 0.35 (others) of the palette per unit of the random offset
moved.reason: The second measurement was +2.7% hue entropy (3.670 to 3.769 bits) against the +5% bound: the right direction but weak, because the full-frame hue histogram is already close to saturated. Dispersion is a named part of the high band's grammar and should be visible, so the strength was raised; the +5% bound is unchanged.

moved.check: bass hit: compression (design strengthened, criterion unchanged)
moved.reason: The first measurement was a 2.5% fall in luminous spread against a 3% bound: the effect existed but was weak (particles near the frame edge are clipped, and sprite sizes do not change). A deep compression pulse should be visible, so the strength was raised; the 3% bound is unchanged.

moved.from: circular hue standard deviation, high 0.3 against 0.9, +10%
moved.to: hue entropy, dispersion 0 against 0.9 at the same visibility, +5%
moved.reason: See the note above the list: the first probe confounded visibility with dispersion, the second used a metric that is not monotonic in colour variety (43.0 to 38.3 degrees with the dispersion on).

moved.from: identical frame mean and centroid (exact equality)
moved.to: clock, flow, hue and shimmer exactly equal; frame mean within 0.5% and centroid within 0.1% of the frame
moved.reason: Ill-posed: while paused the band envelopes keep easing towards silence by design (the field calms), so pixels change by a few parts in a thousand for several seconds. The quantities that must hold still (the visual clock and the flow phase) are still asserted exactly.
